Releases are unminified with no source maps; the Marketplace scanners have removed minified bundles before. .vscode-test.mjs calls the package build 'minified', which disagrees with this. Defines: BEETHOVEN_BUILD, BEETHOVEN_VERSION and __BEETHOVEN_TEST_KEYS__ (test builds add a committed test signing key; a production build refuses --tests and refuses an empty grid/license_keys.json). esbuild also copies every grid/ file except *.d.ts into dist/grid with CRLF turned to LF; the wizard scp's them to ~/.beethoven/bin and runs `beethoven install`. build-meta/*.json metafiles feed tools/third_party_notices.mjs. Runtime dependencies are bundled: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.30.1, ssh2 1.17.0, zod 4.6.5. Tests: unit tests with `node --test` over dist-test/unit (esbuild --tests compiles every *.test.ts outside vscode-test). Integration tests with @vscode/test-cli 0.0.15, @vscode/test-electron 3.1.0 and mocha 11.7.1 (tdd): labels unit (temporary BEETHOVEN_LICENSE_DIR), live (whole graph against the real grid) and package (unpacked release). Container-only tests (phone.test, daemon.test) run on a real worker allocation through tools/grid_tests.sh. CI: the repository has no .github/workflows. .github holds only dependabot.yml (npm weekly for /extension, actions), CODEOWNERS and a PR template that asks for diagnostic nodes and REQUIRED_BY_FEATURE. Release is tools/release.mjs: esbuild --production, notices, vsce package, release_check.mjs (also unpacks for the package tests), then SHA256SUMS signed with the licence key from BEETHOVEN_VENDOR_DIR. tools/publish_marketplace.sh. Push with tools/push_org.sh or push_via_grid.sh. Grid side: no build step. Bash plus coreutils on the login node; Node runs only inside the container. Nothing of hpcworker is used or vendored (no profiles, no framework, no V11 contract), and no site profile exists: Wayne State values are hardcoded in package.json defaults, wizard.ts, slurm.ts, services.ts, diagReport.ts, bashrc.block and grid/beethoven. Shared infrastructure that lives in this repository but serves both editions: tools/intake/worker.js, the Cloudflare Worker access, licence and report service (about 1,900 lines, wrangler.toml, worker.test.mjs, the same code deployed as beethoven-access and ashley-service; /trial issues VS Code keys, access_check answers the browser edition). Also tools/license/beethoven-license.mjs, the issuer, which signs keys, revocation lists, release sums and the browser edition's kill-list. Logic copied by hand across files and editions, and so a natural candidate for a shared base: the credential variable list (services.ts CLAUDE_CREDENTIAL_ENV = beethovend.js AUTH_VARS = phone.js AUTH_VARS = the env -u lists in grid/beethoven and login_relay.sh); the subscription test (wizard.ts localClaudeStatus = beethovend.js and phone.js isSubscription, like hpcworker hpcw_claude_signin); RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS and parseResetTime (protocol.ts = beethovend.js); the .claude.json seed (grid/beethoven claude_in_alloc = login_relay.sh = phone.js trust seed). Clients: cli/beethoven and cli/beethoven.ps1 (ssh forwarders to the grid command, with old-name copies cli/ashley and cli/ashley.ps1).

modules.purpose: The stdio entry point Claude Desktop or Claude Code starts. It reads the settings (configFrom), loads the site profile, builds one Grid and the twelve tools, and serves MCP on stdin/stdout. If the profile cannot be read, it still serves a grid_check that explains why, plus account_list. If the settings have problems, every grid tool answers with them as an error, while account_list keeps working. It writes one fixed stderr line ('beethoven-desktop 1.0.0 started'). It also holds the INSTRUCTIONS text sent to the model. Tests: test/mcp.e2e.test.ts spawns the compiled server/index.js through the official MCP SDK client and checks the twelve tools, the instructions, the stderr line, the missing-profile fallback and the placeholder account.

modules.purpose: This edition's mirror of the cluster seam. It holds the name, site and account regexes; the Claude Code link regexes and their exact-match test; the gate lines (GateLine to SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND, and the remote line `env SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND='...' bash '<shared>/bin/hpcworker' gate`); and parsers for gate refusals and limits, the `HPCW-GATE ok` version line, the `status NAME` JSON line (StatusJson with status/connection/scheduler), HPCW-STEP lines, progress.log lines and the 'worker NAME: stopped (' line. It also holds linkOf, which prefers the environment link over the session link. Differences from the other repositories, relevant to a shared base: (1) FAIL_CODES lacks framework 17's 'signin-billed' and 'signin-method' (in V11_CONTRACT.md lines 64-65 and in the extension's StepFailCode), so both parse here as 'other'. (2) WORKER_NAME_RE is the gate's gate_name_ok (leading alphanumeric), stricter than the extension's internal /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$/. (3) There is no isEnvironmentUrl. (4) isClaudeCodeLink takes unknown, where the extension's takes string | undefined. Tests: test/unit.test.ts 'the gate lines'; test/grid.ssh.test.ts against test/gate-standin.sh and, with HPCWORKER_DIR, the real hpcworker gate; test/mcp.e2e.test.ts.

modules.purpose: A hand-written MCP server over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line). It handles initialize (version negotiation), ping, tools/list (annotations carry the title) and tools/call. Notifications and responses are ignored. Lines are capped at 4 MiB. A tool's own exception becomes an isError result: ArgError's message, or 'Beethoven hit an error it did not expect. Nothing was changed on the grid by this request.'. serveStdio wires it to process stdin/stdout. Tests: test/unit.test.ts 'MCP over stdio, in process'; test/mcp.e2e.test.ts (official @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0 client against the compiled server).

modules.purpose: Read-only view of the student's own Claude accounts on this computer, as the engine's account switcher bee keeps them. It reads <registry>/accounts.json (at most 64 KiB) and <registry>/usage/<label>.json (at most 4 KiB) and nothing else. The registry is $BEE_REGISTRY_DIR, else <$BEETHOVEN_HOME or ~/.beethoven>/engine. readSmall refuses a link or an oversized file by LSTAT. The rows match 'bee account list --json': order, resting_until, 5-hour and 7-day usage while the window lasts. describeAccounts writes the plain-word view. modules.purpose: worker_list's data: every worker of the account, read over sftp from <state_dir>/<name>/status.json only. It skips 'workspaces', links and names that fail WORKER_NAME_RE, caps the count at 100, and caps each status file at 64 KiB with plain-file LSTAT and FSTAT checks. rowOf treats the file as untrusted: word() strips control characters and caps lengths, and a link is kept only if isClaudeCodeLink passes. Each row carries the Claude account (email) and plan the worker reported. No gate line and no scheduler call. modules.purpose: The Grid class: everything a tool may ask of the grid, and how often. It handles the sign-in (a terminal launcher, then a wait of up to 40 s for the ControlMaster), sign-out (ssh -O exit), and the gate verbs version, status, connect, stop and read progress.log, each as one ssh over the kept sign-in. Calls go through a Serial queue, with the host key pinned before every call. Workspace list/read and worker listing go over an sftp child, and openInClaude hands the link to the OS opener. Floors: status once per 60 s per worker (cached answer with as-of and next times); start/stop once per 60 s; log, workspace and list reads once per 5 s. It maps ssh failures, gate refusals and limits (names, hourly, watch/busy, expired key, 126/127 not on the approved list) to plain sentences, including a VPN hint from the profile. Deps are injectable for tests. Tests: test/grid.ssh.test.ts throughout, against a real sshd on 127.0.0.1 (test/lab.ts) with test/gate-standin.sh, and with HPCWORKER_DIR the real hpcworker gate; test/mcp.e2e.test.ts.
exports: Grid (route, signedIn, signIn, signOut, version, status, start, stop, log, list, read, workers, openInClaude)
modules.platform: node:child_process (spawn for the sftp child; otherwise ssh.ts/terminal.ts)
modules.contract_or_rules: Grid etiquette: on the grid only the gate's own lines plus sshd's sftp-server; status at most once a minute (the gate's --poll-floor 60 is a second floor behind it); starts and stops at most once a minute. connect never signs in to Claude. Nothing is deleted anywhere. Only a checked Claude Code link is opened. Students see plain words.

modules.purpose: Spawns the student's own OpenSSH. routeFor picks the route: native ssh, Windows' System32 OpenSSH without multiplexing, or wsl.exe -e ssh with the socket in WSL's own home. It also covers argv for the interactive sign-in (ControlMaster=auto, ControlPersist 4h), BatchMode calls (-T, never a prompt), the sftp subsystem (-s ... sftp) and control checks; ssh-keyscan -4; run() with shell:false, a timeout and output caps; classify() of ssh's exit 255 into not-installed, not-signed-in, hostkey, unreachable, timeout or ssh; Serial; and host-key pinning (fingerprintOf, pinnedLines, ensurePinned writes only lines whose key matches the profile's fingerprint to ~/.beethoven-desktop/known_hosts, mode 0600, no trust on first use). childEnv drops credential-named variables from every child. Tests: test/unit.test.ts 'ssh' (pinning, argv per route, wslPath, childEnv with all nine key routes, classify); test/grid.ssh.test.ts (wrong host key refused, BatchMode never prompts, sign-in outlives its window, sign-out); test/lab.ts uses fingerprintOf.
modules.contract_or_rules: No secret in argv or a file: the grid password and code go only to ssh's own prompt, with no askpass, sshpass or expect. Host key pinned from the site profile with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes; no agent, X11 or port forwarding; PermitLocalCommand=no. MACs=+hmac-sha1 and AddressFamily=inet were measured by the VS Code edition (sshConfig.ts, 2026-09-28). DROP_ENV removes ANTHROPIC_*, CLAUDE_CODE_*, CLAUDECODE, AI_AGENT and *TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/API_KEY* names; that line is a forbidden.mjs STRIP_SITE (no API key anywhere). spawn with shell:false only.

modules.purpose: A read-only SFTP v3 client (draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-02) over an `ssh -s host sftp` child. Requests: INIT/VERSION, REALPATH, LSTAT, FSTAT, OPENDIR, READDIR, OPEN (read only), READ and CLOSE. readFile takes a check callback that sees FSTAT before any byte is read. It skips shell text printed ahead of the VERSION reply (a ~/.bashrc that prints) up to 64 KiB, caps packets at 512 KiB and reads in 32 KiB chunks. Tests: no direct unit test. Covered by test/grid.ssh.test.ts 'the workspace, over sftp' (including a ~/.bashrc that prints and "the file session is sshd's sftp subsystem, and started no command") and by the worker-list tests; test/mcp.e2e.test.ts workspace_read.
exports: Sftp (start, realpath, lstat, readdir, readFile, close, lastStderr)
modules.contract_or_rules: Nothing is deleted: no request that writes, renames or removes exists. No shell command of ours runs on the login node, since sshd's own sftp-server does the work.

modules.purpose: Path rules for reading the worker's own folder, <state_dir>/workspaces/<name>, over sftp. segmentsOf refuses absolute paths, '.', '..', control characters and over-long paths. The directory is resolved on the grid by REALPATH and must lie inside the workspace's resolved root. A file must be plain by LSTAT (a link is refused, not followed), and the FSTAT size and mtime must still match at open. Credential-named files are refused: .credentials.json, .claude.json, job.token, *.token, .netrc, .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_*. A NUL in the first 8 KiB marks a file binary, and nothing of it is shown. Text passes redactCredentials. Limits: read 256 KiB by default, 1 MiB at most; listings of 500 entries. Tests: test/unit.test.ts "the workspace's path rules" (refusedName, segmentsOf); test/grid.ssh.test.ts 'the workspace, over sftp' (planted links, credential names, path tricks, binary file) and the real-framework workspace listing.
modules.contract_or_rules: Never a Claude credential: credential-named files are refused, and this is the only file allowed to name '.credentials.json' (the forbidden.mjs EXCEPTIONS entry). Workspace reads stay inside the workspace by the grid's own REALPATH and never follow a link. Credential-shaped text is redacted.

modules.purpose: Writes the sign-in launcher (sign-in.sh, sign-in.command or sign-in.cmd, mode 0700, atomic rename) into ~/.beethoven-desktop: three plain sentences and the ssh line, with shQuote/cmdQuote quoting. terminalArgv opens it in a terminal: macOS Terminal, Windows `cmd /c start`, or the first Linux terminal found on PATH. openerArgv refuses any text that is not a Claude Code link and uses open, rundll32 url.dll or xdg-open. launch() starts a program detached, with childEnv and shell:false. Tests: test/unit.test.ts 'the sign-in launcher' (quoting, a '%' path refused on Windows, no terminal found); test/grid.ssh.test.ts (launch through the lab's fake terminal; 'a link that is not a Claude Code link is never opened'); test/mcp.e2e.test.ts grid_sign_in.
modules.contract_or_rules: The grid password and one-time code are typed only into ssh's own prompt in a window the student sees; the launcher holds no secret. No code on claude.ai: one checked claude.ai/code link is handed to the OS opener, and nothing else touches claude.ai. Students see plain words.

modules.purpose: Builds dist/beethoven/, which is both a Claude Desktop extension and a Claude Code plugin. It refuses to build unless package.json, bundle/manifest.json, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and src/version.ts carry the same N.0.0 version. It runs tsc -p tsconfig.build.json into server/, copies profiles/*.json (each checked as JSON), the manifest, icon, .claude-plugin, skills and README, and writes a minimal package.json {type: module}. It then runs forbidden.mjs on the compiled server. With --pack it runs mcpb validate and pack, producing dist/beethoven-<v>.mcpb. Tests: CI and the pre-push gate run `npm run pack`; test/mcp.e2e.test.ts compiles its own copy with tsc instead.

modules.purpose: The posture check run on src and on the built server. Imports are limited to node:child_process, crypto, fs, os, path and url, and child_process may supply only spawn. It refuses: fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and EventSource; eval and new Function; exec, execFile, fork and shell:true; sshpass, expect, PasswordAuthentication, SSH_ASKPASS and KbdInteractive; setup-token, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and auth logout; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN/BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_FILE_DESCRIPTOR and USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY, apiKeyHelper, console.anthropic.com, platform.claude.com, sk-ant- and --console; ~/.claude, .beethoven/claude, .ashley/claude and claude_config_dir; rmSync, unlink, rmdir and fs.rm; console.*; and the gate verbs forget, watch and restrict. STRIP_SITES allow key names only on ssh.ts's single DROP_ENV regex line and on redact.ts rule lines. EXCEPTIONS allow '.credentials.json' only in workspace.ts. Tests: test/unit.test.ts 'the posture check' checks a clean source, the strips passing, and planted routes failing.

design.recommendation: beethoven-base should be a small TypeScript library with no platform code, about 2,800 lines of logic that exist two or three times today across roughly 34,000 lines of client code. It holds four kinds of thing. (1) The client half of hpcworker's contract: the parsers for HPCW-STEP, LOGIN, GATE and KEY lines, progress.log, status.json and connection.json, the gate's verbs and answers, the validated command lines a client sends, and the run rules R1 to R13 (which link to open, when a heartbeat counts as stale). (2) The rules every edition must apply the same way: the subscription-only sign-in test (including apiKeySource), the list of credential, gateway and provider variables to strip, redaction, the per-class etiquette floors, the account and worker name rules, and the Claude Code link check. (3) Logic that is the same everywhere: the site profile reader with the profiles as data, the diagnostics engine, the core of the terms record, the signed-list verifier, the reader for the engine's accounts.json, OpenSSH options and host-key pinning, and one plain sentence per contract outcome. (4) Two tools: a vendor/vendor-check script and the posture scan. Each edition keeps everything that is UI, platform API, transport, packaging or legal text. The browser edition keeps the portal client, the native-messaging bridge, its own SSH client, the keyring, the approval check and its panel. Desktop keeps the MCP server, ControlMaster/WSL, the SFTP client and its manifests. VS Code keeps the VS Code API surfaces, its licence keys on the laptop, error reports, Remote-SSH and its wizard. Each edition takes base as a pinned copy inside its own source root (extension/src/base, src/base, extension/src/base), checked against an ORIGIN record by a hash check that needs no secret, and its existing bundler or compiler builds that copy into what ships. The VS Code edition is moved explicitly onto hpcworker, so the three editions drive one cluster side. Two things are greg's decisions: whether hpcworker grows the `claude -p` request queue (my recommendation) or VS Code drops it, and dropping the grid-side licence check. Students already on grid scripts 8 keep their sign-in directory untouched. The profile's claude_config_dir is that same folder, so they do not sign in again.

design.consumption:
Recommendation: a pinned vendored copy with a hash check, and no secret in any edition.

**Where the copy goes.** It lives inside each edition's own source root, so the toolchain that edition already has builds it and nothing else changes:
- beethoven-extension: extension/src/base/. WXT/Vite bundles it.
- beethoven-desktop: src/base/. The same tsc that builds the server compiles it into dist/beethoven/server/base/.
- beethoven-vscode: extension/src/base/. esbuild bundles it into dist/extension.js, dist/mcp-server.js and dist/beethoven-cli.js, unminified as now.

**What the copy holds.** The TypeScript modules, the profiles as data, ORIGIN, and vendor-check.mjs. There are no tests (they stay in base) and no package.json: a "type" field there would turn VS Code's Node16 files into ESM.

**Same model as beethoven-qa.** beethoven-research carries vendor/beethoven-qa with ORIGIN (repository, ref v1.0.0, commit 16415b4, tree_sha256, files), runs `pixi run --locked vendor-check` in CI and pre-push, and refuses hand edits. The two kit files it carries are byte-equal to the copy's. Base keeps the same ORIGIN fields and digest, in a Node twin of the script.

**Rules the base source keeps, so all three editions can build it:**
- Modules import only each other, through relative `.js` specifiers.
- No import.meta, no top-level await, no require, no node: or DOM imports, no fetch, no eval.
- Hashing and Ed25519 go through globalThis.crypto.subtle.
- Bytes are typed Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>.

**Measured in scratch** (/tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/c7a8e2b5-aaa7-5d66-b7b7-e67a1565c5b8/scratchpad/basex), using each repository's own installed toolchain:
- One such source compiled and ran under desktop's NodeNext ESM tsc, VS Code's Node16 CommonJS tsc plus esbuild (Ed25519 verify true on Node 22), and the extension's Bundler/verbatimModuleSyntax/noUncheckedIndexedAccess tsc with vitest and vite build.
- With the DOM lib, TypeScript 5.9.3 rejects Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> as a BufferSource. So base's CI must typecheck in all three configurations, with the union of the editions' flags.

**What ships.** Everything is bundled or compiled at build time, so no student build and no store package ever needs a token.
- Desktop's server still imports only node: modules; base's files are its own relative imports, and forbidden.mjs's ALLOWED_IMPORTS is unchanged.
- The browser extension loads nothing remote.
- VS Code ships no new dependency.

**Weighed against fetching base at a pinned commit in CI with a fine-grained token** (Contents read on beethoven-base, or a read-only deploy key):
- Every place that builds would need a credential: each edition's CI as a secret, greg's Mac release script, and every cloud session (base attached).
- A git dependency, npm package or submodule from a private repository also needs credentials on every `npm ci` or clone.
- An edition's pull request would show only a commit bump, so what an edition ships would not be in its own history or its review diff.
- A build would fail when GitHub or the token is unavailable or expired.

The vendored copy costs about 3,000 duplicated lines per edition, plus one pull request per edition per base release. A bot opens those (below), and vendor-check refuses any hand edit. It is a check in the consumer, not a proof: an edit that also rewrites ORIGIN passes it, and `check --source` from base's own checkout closes that gap, as in beethoven-qa.

**The one credential the design uses** is optional, and it lives only in beethoven-base. greg allowed CI secrets at 20:14Z. BASE_PROPAGATE_TOKEN is a fine-grained token:
- Repositories beethoven-extension, beethoven-desktop and beethoven-vscode.
- Contents and Pull requests read and write. No Workflows: the copy never touches .github, so none is needed.
- Kept as a repository secret of beethoven-base.

`.github/workflows/propagate.yml` runs on a published base release, in a matrix over the three editions:
1. Check out base at the tag with the default token, and the edition with the secret through actions/checkout's `token` input (an extraheader, not argv).
2. Run `node tools/vendor.mjs vendor --into <edition>/<dir>` and the anchored `check --source .`.
3. Push the branch base/v<N> and run `gh pr create` with GH_TOKEN taken from the secret in env. Nothing is echoed, no secret is in argv or a log, and it never runs on pull_request_target.

A pull request opened with a token (unlike GITHUB_TOKEN) starts the edition's own CI, and each edition's automerge.yml merges it on green where its ruleset is applied. Desktop has both files today. The extension (only ci.yml) and VS Code (no workflows) wait for greg's merge until they adopt the kit.

Without the token, a session runs the same vendor command and opens the pull requests with its own sign-in.

RULESETS_TOKEN (Administration, for rulesets) is used only by base's rulesets.yml, never to read or write code. No Claude or Anthropic key is involved anywhere: no workflow runs Claude Code, and the no-API-key rule stands unchanged.

**CLAUDE.md lines each pull request must change.** Under this design the editions' CI still holds no secret, so these lines stay true in substance and only gain the copy and its check:
- beethoven-extension CLAUDE.md:308 ("No secrets exist in this repository and the workflow needs none"): add that the pinned beethoven-base copy under extension/src/base is checked by vendor-check, which needs none.
- beethoven-extension CLAUDE.md:300-303: the profiles now come from the base copy, not framework/profiles/pull.sh.
- beethoven-extension CLAUDE.md:185: sync-profiles reads extension/src/base/profiles.
- beethoven-desktop CLAUDE.md:89 ("CI ... holds no secret"): add vendor-check.
- beethoven-desktop CLAUDE.md:42-43 ("the server's only imports are Node's own modules ... no dependency at run time"): add "and the pinned copy of beethoven-base in src/base, compiled with it".
- beethoven-desktop CLAUDE.md:72 (profiles/pull.sh): the profiles come from src/base/profiles.
- hpcworker CLAUDE.md:298-303: beethoven-base carries the pinned contract, vectors and profiles, and the one client implementation.

If greg chose the fetch route instead, extension:308 and desktop:89 would have to say that CI holds a read token for beethoven-base. The no-API-key bullets (extension:58, hpcworker:58, desktop:31) would need a clause that a GitHub credential for code is not a Claude key or token.
design.contract_home:
**What stays canonical in hpcworker.** hpcworker stays canonical for the server side, because the writer is the authority on what it writes. It keeps:
- docs/V11_CONTRACT.md, docs/V12_CONTRACT.md (and V13 if the request queue moves).
- The writer itself.
- framework/profiles/*.json with their schema and CLI (framework/lib/profile.py).
- New machine-readable vectors under docs/contract/vectors/. These are lines and files produced by the suite from the real writer: every D9 failure code including signin-billed and signin-method, `HPCW-STEP signed-in - -`, status.json and connection.json for each of R1 to R13 including a session_url-only online, the gate's answers and exit codes, the CLEAN_ENV list, and `claude auth status` cases including apiKeySource. A Python 3.6 unittest fails when the writer and the vectors differ.

**Text fixes in the same hpcworker pull request:**
- V11_CONTRACT.md line 722 and R5 still say both URL fields hold the environment link "as framework 9" and that online needs environment_url. Framework 14 changed this, so the text lags its own code.
- The helper wire table in V12 is the extension's own contract with its bridge, and its two copies already differ (hpcworker says kind 'script', the extension 'script|binary'). It moves to beethoven-extension.

**What beethoven-base holds.** A pinned copy of those texts, vectors and profiles (hpcworker/ with an ORIGIN naming the hpcworker commit and tree digest), and the one client implementation. Base's CI parses every vector and fails when one does not parse to its expected value.

**What the editions retire.** They take the profiles and the parsers from base only, and retire their own copies:
- beethoven-extension: framework/profiles with pull.sh, and docs/V11_CONTRACT.md and docs/V12_CONTRACT.md.
- beethoven-desktop: profiles/ with pull.sh.
- beethoven-vscode: never had any.

That is one path instead of three, and the drift found today (desktop's parsers, the V12 line) has nowhere left to live.

**How they stay in step.** Everything flows one way, hpcworker to base to editions:
1. A contract change is one hpcworker pull request: text, writer and vectors, with framework N+1, published to the lab's shared copy with deploy_shared.sh. The shared copy keeps older numbered versions, and a running chain keeps its code.
2. Then one base pull request re-pulls at that commit with `node tools/pull-hpcworker.mjs`, which is pull.sh's logic over the person's own gh sign-in. Optionally a workflow in hpcworker does this, holding a token with Contents and Pull requests write on beethoven-base. The pull request changes the parsers until every vector passes, and a release follows.
3. The propagation pull requests carry it to the editions.

**Version check.** Base exports FRAMEWORK_MIN, the oldest framework whose output its parsers accept: 17 now, higher once a later framework is required. Each edition reads the lab copy's version (gate `version` or `hpcworker version`) and says, in plain words, that the lab's copy needs an update when the copy is older. That closes a gap: today no edition enforces a minimum, and the extension's FRAMEWORK_CONNECT_VERSION = 10 is referenced nowhere.

**The fourth-repository idea** for the grid's rules and profiles (REPO_SPLIT.md section 2, undecided) is not pre-empted. Base could later be that home for the JSON, but then hpcworker (bash, Python 3.6) and beethoven-agents (Python) would take their profiles from a TypeScript repository and the arrow would reverse. Until greg decides, hpcworker stays the home, as REPO_SPLIT.md says.

Publish VS Code 7.0.0 on the Marketplace and tell VS Code students one thing: their Claude sign-in stays, one click moves their worker to the lab's copy, and nothing of theirs on the grid is deleted.
risks: Base becomes a coupling point. A release that changes a parser fails each edition at typecheck, which is the point. But an edition that stays on an old base brings drift back, so the propagation pull requests and vendor-check's refusal of hand edits must actually be used.

Three module systems build one source. Measured in scratch: it works under NodeNext ESM, Node16 CommonJS with esbuild, and Bundler with Vite. But TypeScript 5.9.3's DOM lib rejects Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> as a BufferSource while Node's types accept it. Base's CI must typecheck all three lanes with the union of the editions' flags, and the copy must carry no package.json 'type'.

The editions' posture checks run over base once it is vendored: desktop's forbidden.mjs (only node: imports, no fetch, credential names only on strip lines) and the extension's hygiene test (old name only in allowed files, plain words). Base must pass the strictest settings first, or a base release turns an edition red.

Shared fixes change what students see. Desktop opens the resumed session rather than an environment link and warns at 3 minutes instead of 5. A Console-key sign-in stops working in every client, which is intended. Each edition's pull request must say so, and the edition's version goes up.

Not yet measured: a VS Code phone host (phone.js) and an hpcworker Remote Control worker on one sign-in, and an old claude -p daemon beside Remote Control on another node, may contend for the same OAuth credential. The move stops the old worker first, but both can run until the student clicks, as they can today.

Commands that delete stay on the grid. Grid scripts up to 8 have `uninstall`, which runs rm -rf on the real ~/.beethoven including claude/, the sign-in directory hpcworker also uses, and `claude forget`. A person at a terminal can still run them on any account that never updates. Step 5 makes grid scripts 9 keep the sign-in, and nothing in the migration ever calls them.

Two access models write ACLs on one volume. VS Code's `access init` closes shared/ to other, and `access admin approve` adds root entries that grid_access.sh removes when the student is not on its list. VS Code-only students could be cut off before or during the move unless the list includes them (step 14). Where `admin.mjs roster` lives is not established: grid_access.sh calls it, but this checkout's admin.mjs has no such command.

Workspace continuity: hpcworker's worker uses a new folder, so Claude Code's --continue does not find conversations made under ~/.beethoven's workspaces. They are kept, not moved, and students must be told.

If the request queue moves into hpcworker under its etiquette (no 250 ms loop on the login node, bounded waits), ask latency rises from about one network round trip to seconds. How much is not yet measured.

Ed25519 through WebCrypto verified on Node 22 here. On the VS Code extension host's Electron it is not yet measured. Until it is, VS Code can keep node:crypto for the issuer and grid/license.js for the laptop.

BASE_PROPAGATE_TOKEN is the one standing credential that can write code in three repositories. Scope it to those three, give it an expiry, keep it only in beethoven-base, trigger only on published releases, and never use pull_request_target.

The writer stays bash and Python 3.6 and the parsers stay TypeScript. They remain two implementations checked against one set of vectors, so drift is caught, not prevented, and only as far as the vectors reach.

Base saves less than 'add features to all of them' suggests: about 2,800 lines of shared logic against roughly 34,000 lines of client code. Most of a visible feature is still three UI, platform and transport implementations.

Texts: moving VS Code onto hpcworker changes what runs on the grid (no licence check there, the lab's shared copy, an always-on Remote Control worker), so its LICENSE and PRIVACY texts and TERMS_VERSION must change together, to 7. The browser and desktop texts are not changed by adopting base.

In-flight conflicts: extension 15.0.0 touches helper/ and release/, so the overlap is low. VS Code wip/account's core/accounts.ts is replaced by base's reader. hpcworker's open queue-report branch must merge before step 7 so the vectors come from its main branch.

problems: Base fails desktop's own posture check, so 'base passes the strictest settings first' cannot hold for the listed contents. I ran /home/claude/beethoven-desktop/scripts/forbidden.mjs over a copy of the extension's contract.ts, the source the design names for gate.ts, links.ts, commands.ts and files.ts. It reported 8 findings: CONSOLE_SIGNIN_HOST = 'platform.claude.com' (isClaudeAuthUrl), the probe verdict's platform.claude.com egress lines, and `watch ${name}`, `restrict ${name}`, forget: () => 'forget' and GateLimit 'watch'. That last rule is labelled 'a gate verb this edition never sends'. It is a deliberate desktop posture: desktop CLAUDE.md says only version/status/connect/stop/read run. STRIP_SITES also allows credential names only on a single-line `const DROP_ENV = /…/;` in a file named ssh.ts or redact.ts, so a list in src/rules/credentials.ts fails too. To fix it, either weaken desktop's rule (which needs a decision) or keep these out of what desktop compiles. The design names neither.

The size claim is not backed by the overlap. The ~2,800 figure equals the sum of the overlap's per-concern loc (2,810). That sum includes the consent signal (40), which the overlap says belongs in hpcworker and the design does not move, plus posture tooling (120) and accounts (180). A file-size estimate of the second and third copies base would actually replace before VS Code moves comes to roughly 850 lines: about 540 in desktop (contract, redact, profile, account parsing, rowOf, floors, describeSteps, ssh options and pin) and about 300 in VS Code (diagnostics engine, terms core, subscription test, strip list, account parsing, ssh options). Most of base's 2,800 lines would be the extension's own code with the extension as the only full consumer. The 34,000 total is right: 24,947 + 6,850 + 2,579.

Several modules are shared in name only and have one real consumer.
- parseLoginLine, LOGIN_LINES and isClaudeAuthUrl serve the browser's plain-mode sitting. Desktop runs `hpcworker claude login` in the student's own terminal and the gate is always --login never. VS Code would do the same after its move.
- HPCW-KEY lines, gate forget/watch and the browser-key added lines belong to the browser key's lifecycle.
- probeVerdict and ProbeFile: only the extension probes.

- The apiKeySource rule is vacuous in the extension. The framework writes only {loggedIn,email,subscriptionType} to status.json and {loggedIn,subscriptionType,email,authMethod} to probe.json (worker.sbatch.tpl check_auth, probe.sbatch:159), so the field never reaches the client. Base's own source rules (no node: imports, hashing through WebCrypto) push platform assumptions onto the editions.
- VS Code's terms hashing is synchronous node:crypto (core/terms.ts:120), used inside the synchronous record build at extension.ts:778 and in termsPanel.ts:33. It would have to become async.
- Desktop's fingerprintOf is sync createHash, used by pinnedLines and ensurePinned.
- routeFor uses node:path posix/win32, homedir and process.platform, so it cannot live in base at all.

credentials.ts, as designed, would take a feature away from VS Code. Desktop's DROP_ENV (/…|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|API_?KEY/i, src/ssh.ts:156) is meant to be the outer net. (a) accounts.json is written by beethoven-research src/beethoven_research/bee/accounts.py, yet the design names no canonical writer and no vectors for it. run.ts calls a deliberate desktop choice 'drift'. desktop src/contract.ts linkOf is commented 'the environment link first (a new session can start there)'. Making base impose session-first on desktop is a product decision for greg, not a bug fix.

The students at risk are those approved only on the grid through `access admin approve` (status files under shared/access), which the service never sees. framework 18's cross-edition effects are understated.
- `hpcworker env set` loads VS Code's GitHub and Hugging Face tokens into every worker of the account, including browser-started Remote Control sessions whose transcripts go to Anthropic. That contradicts 'browser and desktop texts are not changed'.
- editor_env and node_domain put VS Code Remote-SSH specifics into the shared profile schema, which every edition pins.
- names.ts folds two different identities into one account_pattern: the portal's dashboard identity (the extension's /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._@-]{0,63}$/, which can be user@domain elsewhere) and the unix login.

Desktop's posture scan rejects base as specified (measured). Running beethoven-desktop/scripts/forbidden.mjs over the extension modules that base takes gives 8 findings. They are contract.ts:293 CONSOLE_SIGNIN_HOST='platform.claude.com' (isClaudeAuthUrl), contract.ts:801-805 (probe egress text naming platform.claude.com) and contract.ts:986/994/1008/1061 (the gate verbs 'watch', 'restrict' and 'forget', which desktop refuses as verbs it never sends). A credentials.ts strip list in the one-pattern-per-line form also fails: STRIP_SITES is keyed by basename (ssh.ts, redact.ts) and accepts only a line that is literally `const DROP_ENV = /.../;`, so `export const CLEAN_ENV = /.../` fails twice. A vendor-check.mjs placed in src/base fails the default `npm run forbidden` scan of src because it prints (console.log and console.error are refused). tsconfig.build.json includes src/**/*.ts, so tsc compiles every base module into dist/beethoven/server/base and the build's own scan of dist fails as well. The .mcpb would also ship code desktop never imports: the verbs it must never send, the signed-list verifier and the services.json address. 'Base passes the strictest settings first' cannot hold, because base must contain what the extension needs. Fix: build desktop from files:["src/index.ts"] (reachable modules only) and scan only the emitted tree, give base files explicit per-file allowances, and keep vendor-check outside src.

The extension's hygiene test fails on the vendored copy (measured). SRC walks src for .json files, so src/base/profiles/wayne.json becomes part of the old-name test. It fails at line 56 ('$HOME/.beethoven/claude/.ashley-remote-consent') and at line 88 (the notes' '/shared/ashley and', with no trailing slash, so KEPT does not cover it). The planned allowlist entry 'src/base/signed.ts for ASHLEYREV1' is not needed, because KEPT already strips ASHLEYREV1 on every line, and it misses this failure. A required header comment naming VS Code's licence-key code would also trip 'accepts no key' (/licen[cs]e[ -]key/). Step 10 deletes ../framework/profiles, and then the built-package check's profile-set comparison turns itself off without a word (its try/catch returns undefined). sync-profiles.mjs only warns when its source folder is missing. A package that ships with no site profile would then pass every test.

BASE_PROPAGATE_TOKEN is exposed to more than the workflow that uses it, and can do more than open pull requests. As a repository secret of beethoven-base it is available to every push and same-repository pull_request workflow there. Base's kit (step 6) auto-merges on green with no review, and sessions push branches there. So any branch that edits a workflow, or a step-13 propagate.yml that itself lands by auto-merge, can use a token that writes code in three repositories. It is greg's fine-grained token, so it carries the OrganizationAdmin bypass (bypass_mode 'always' in desktop's .github/rulesets/main.json; not measured with a PAT) and can push straight to main past the required checks. The extension and VS Code have no ruleset at all, and Contents write cannot be limited to pull-request branches. Fix: keep it as an Environment secret, deployable only from v* tags with greg as reviewer (the org already enforces rulesets on private repositories, so environments should be available), or use a GitHub App identity that is not on the bypass list. Use persist-credentials only for the push step, and never run the edition's npm ci or scripts in that job.

RULESETS_TOKEN can do more than the design and the hand-off say. greg made it an organisation secret visible to all repositories (20:14Z), so a same-repository pull_request workflow in any OpenSpineConsortium repository can read it. Fine-grained Administration write also covers deploy keys (a write deploy key can push code), repository visibility and the rulesets themselves (GitHub's permission model; not exercised here). 'Used only by base's rulesets.yml, never to read or write code', and 'manages settings and cannot read code' (told to greg at 20:17Z and recorded in state/repos/beethoven-base.md), describe how it is used, not what it can do. The greg step adds beethoven-base to its coverage anyway. Fix: per-repository Environment secrets limited to main for rulesets.yml.

Wording conflict with the no-API-key bullet. hpcworker's and the extension's CLAUDE.md say 'no CI on a key or a token held as a secret', with no 'that runs Claude Code' qualifier (desktop's text has one). Base will hold two GitHub tokens as secrets, and its CLAUDE.md 'restates the non-negotiables'. The design adds the clarifying clause only under the fetch route it rejects. The optional hpcworker workflow with write rights on beethoven-base contradicts hpcworker CLAUDE.md 'CI runs in three lanes, none holding a secret', and that line is missing from the design's list of CLAUDE.md lines to change.

Editions can end up on different base versions with nothing to flag it. Nothing records or compares which base each edition carries. A propagation pull request that fails in one edition just stays open, and the extension and VS Code (no auto-merge) wait for greg indefinitely. vendor-check accepts a downgrade (files and ORIGIN from an older release, for example from step 10's rebase onto 15.0.0 taking the old side) and a hand-rewritten ORIGIN. `vendor --into` 'never deletes', so a module removed or renamed in base either stays compiled into desktop (tsc compiles every file) or turns the automated pull request red until someone deletes it by hand. Fix: vendor removes files the previous ORIGIN listed, check refuses a ref older than main's ORIGIN, a scheduled base job (same environment-protected token, Contents read) reports each edition's ORIGIN and fails when one lags, and each edition shows its base version in its diagnostics.

Base's strip list would break VS Code's token feature. credentials.ts is specified as CLEAN_ENV plus desktop's DROP_ENV prefix net (/TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|API_?KEY/i, ssh.ts:156) as the outer net. Step 12 puts that list in VS Code's services.ts, but VS Code deliberately exports GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN into Claude Code terminals and the grid (services.ts SERVICES, injectLocally and pushToGrid). The net would strip them. Base needs two exports: the exact Claude and provider list (plus the ANTHROPIC_ and CLAUDE_CODE_ prefixes) for every child that runs Claude Code, and the all-secrets net only for desktop's ssh children.

Step 15b's `hpcworker env set NAME` must refuse credential names outright: CLEAN_ENV's names plus the ANTHROPIC_* and CLAUDE_CODE_* prefixes. Stripping them afterwards is not enough, because the framework would otherwise store a Console key or an OAuth token in ~/.hpcworker/env on request, which breaks 'no API key anywhere' and 'never stores a Claude credential'. Step 18(4)'s token re-send must take only SERVICES ids. VS Code's SecretStorage still holds the retired 'anthropicApiKey' under the same SECRET_PREFIX (services.ts:14 RETIRED_SECRETS, vscode/store.ts:90).

Step 5(c) is not enough to make uninstall safe. Grid scripts 8's cmd_uninstall ends with rm -rf on the real ~/.beethoven, and VS Code 5.0.0's Reset calls it (extension.ts:608). That folder holds more than claude/: it also holds the engine's other sign-ins under ~/.beethoven/accounts/<label>/claude and bee's registry ~/.beethoven/engine (D4; VS Code's own beethoven.account reads that registry). Keeping only claude/ and the workspace root would still delete every other account's sign-in. The scripts' accounts/apikey (retire_apikey, cmd_accounts) also lives in the engine's accounts/ namespace, so an account labelled 'apikey' collides with it. Fix: uninstall removes only what install created (bin/, log, workers/, the bashrc block), never accounts/ or engine/.

Step 3 is wrong that 15.0.0 'touches helper/, release/ and the texts, not core'. wip/signed-merge against HEAD changes core/model.ts, steps.ts, terms.ts (TERMS_VERSION 10), bridge.ts and docs/V12_CONTRACT.md (+82 lines: the copy now names hpcworker as canonical, adds 'Signed installers (15.0.0)' and the rust runtime). The matching hpcworker commit ed94b6b ('the same words as the extension's copy', 20:39Z) exists only as a detached HEAD in the scratch worktree hw-contract, on no branch or remote ref, and step 1 does not list it. Step 7 then moves the helper wire table out of hpcworker's V12, the opposite direction, which would undo what was made byte-identical an hour earlier. Settle the direction before 15.0.0 merges, and put ed94b6b on a branch now.

Step 7's 'framework stays 17' conflicts with the deploy tool. The step changes profile.py and wayne.json, but tools/deploy_shared.sh refuses to republish v17 with different files ('publish them as the next integer version ... or rerun with --replace'). Base would pin 'framework 17' data that differs from the deployed v17, and FRAMEWORK_MIN 17 would name two trees. More broadly, the feature flow moves `current` for every student to framework N+1 before any store or Marketplace build can parse it. Nothing states that changes within v:1 must be additive-only, and FRAMEWORK_MIN is only a lower bound; there is no plain notice that the lab copy is newer than the edition.

Step 14 comes too late. tools/grid_access.sh removes every named root entry that is not on its roster, and it has a scheduled mode. `roster` is not in beethoven-vscode tools/intake/admin.mjs on any branch here (git grep on main and wip/account; the script's default checkout path is the 'ashley' folder). Meanwhile greg is told not to approve VS Code students with `access admin approve`, so no new VS Code-only student can be admitted until step 14, after all the base work. The step does not depend on base: move it, and settling where roster lives, to the front.

The store bundle can carry other editions' strings (measured with the extension's own Vite 8). Vite drops a base module the extension never imports: a CLEAN_ENV module did not appear in the output. It keeps top-level call expressions of a module the extension imports only partly: importing just hostKeyMatches from a base ssh.ts shipped 'MACs=+hmac-sha1' and 'StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'. The reviewer would then see desktop's and VS Code's strings unless base keeps top-level values literal (or marked pure) and splits modules per platform. The extension's built-package test should also scan the bundle for API-key names, which it does not do today.

Desktop's declared runtime is untested for base's hashing rule. Desktop's manifest declares runtimes.node >=18.0.0 and starts `node`. Base's rule sends hashing through globalThis.crypto.subtle, so desktop's synchronous fingerprintOf (ssh.ts:243, createHash) would become async. Node's history puts the global crypto behind --experimental-global-webcrypto before 19.0.0 (not measured here; the scratch build ran only on Node 22). Either keep fingerprintOf in desktop or raise runtimes.node to >=20.

Two smaller consumption gaps. VS Code's .vscodeignore excludes src/**, so step 12's 'read from src/base/profiles/wayne.json' works only as a bundled JSON import (resolveJsonModule is on), which embeds the free-text notes the extension strips; the design should say so. Separately, the beethoven-qa precedent cannot be checked here: no vendor/beethoven-qa or vendor-check exists on any ref of the local beethoven-research checkout (origin/main b7b8650, 07:06Z).

The continuation file contradicts this design. /mnt/project-files/state/repos/beethoven-base.md (20:40Z) still records the fetch route ('each edition's CI fetches the base with one new read-only GitHub token that greg makes') and 'RULESETS_TOKEN ... cannot read code'. With greg near his weekly limit, a successor would build that route or ask greg for the token this design rejects. The hand-off thread needs the vendoring decision and the credential corrections before it closes the file.
critique 1.verdict: The approach holds, but not as written. A pinned copy compiled into each build adds no secret to any edition, puts no Claude or Anthropic key anywhere, loads no code at run time, adds no run-time dependency to desktop and needs no new store permission. As specified, though, it turns both editions' own posture checks red, and I measured both. Desktop's forbidden.mjs refuses the extension's isClaudeAuthUrl host and gate verbs, any strip list outside ssh.ts's DROP_ENV line, and a vendor-check.mjs under src; tsc then ships every base module. The extension's old-name test fails on wayne.json under src/base, and its profile check switches itself off once framework/profiles goes. The one write credential lives where any same-repository branch workflow can use it, and as greg's token it can bypass the required checks. RULESETS_TOKEN, an organisation-wide secret, can do more than the design says.
